transcript: What is stunt casting? There's this really interesting thing that happens whenever you call something a stunt cast with somebody that has previous experience in theatre, that people will jump to their defence of, no, this can't be stunt casting, because they are a theatre performer. But the important thing in calling something a stunt cast is not whether or not they're qualified, it's whether or not casting that person in that role is going to generate publicity for the show. Because while there's really no set definition for stunt casting, everybody from T V. Tropes to Wikipedia to the Oxford Dictionary agree that stunt casting generates publicity for whatever medium it happens to be in, whether that's T V, film, or, of course, theatre. And this, of course, includes any casting of somebody who is not a theatre performer at all, who is being cast in a show to generate publicity because they're a reality T V. Star or a movie star. But even somebody who has a background in theatre, who becomes famous for something else, if they are cast in a show, they are generating publicity for that show that would not have happened if they hadn't gotten famous for that something else. And so their casting is going to generate publicity to people who don't just pay attention to theatre news. And so Dylan Mulvaney, absolutely a theatre performer through and through, has a background in theatre, trained in theatre, performed in theatre before she got Famous, and yet her casting announcement got publicity more so than any other person who has been cast in six because of how famous she is outside of theatre. Same with Whitney Leavitt in Chicago. She has a background in dance. It makes sense for her to be cast in a show that features a lot of dance. But everybody agrees she is a stunt cast because she is primarily known for her reality T V. And social media personas. Other than being on Dancing With the stars, she's not known for dance despite having a background in it. But consistently, when somebody has a background in theatre and their casting is being called a stunt cast, people will get really passionate about jumping to their defence. But ultimately, being a stunt cast is not a bad thing. In fact, it's a great thing, frankly. Win win for the performer who gets to do something that they are trained to do and also for the show that is getting publicity beyond what they would normally get. It's only a bad thing when the stunt casting is not a good match for the role and the person being put into that role just can't do it. But in the case of both Whitney and Dylan, they. They definitely can do it. So great, great casting all the way around.
